miriam: Heads up — seeing ~10-15% p95 latency regression + occasional OOMs after fp8 rollout on gpt-large in the perf cluster. Perf test: 1200 concurrent streams. Profiler snippet below, looks like allocator fragmentation + kernel fallbacks.

miriam: ```
allocator: slabpool v2
reserved_workspace_per_stream: 512MB
soft_reserve: true
free_list: many small holes (8k-64k)
kernel_selector: chosen=fp8_fast, fallback_count=432 -> fp32_slow
kv_cache_dtype: float16 (but upcast_count: 74)
OOMs: 3 across 10 nodes
latency_p95: 210ms (baseline 185ms)
```

raj: :eyes: do you have the kernel selection trace? fallback to fp32 is suspect — if kernels upcast, fp8 wins disappear and workspace pressure increases.

miriam: pasted the short kernel trace above. looks like small-matmul kernels flipping to fp32 for some seq lengths. also noticed many tiny allocations from attention KV writes.

dave: My 2c: 512MB per-stream is aggressive for mixed-precision fp8 workloads. soft_reserve=true forces strong reservations that fragment the slabpool under churn. try soft_reserve=false or dynamic soft-reserve that scales with actual max_seq.

miriam: ran quick experiment: set REDWOOD_ALLOC_SOFT_RESERVE=0 on perf nodes and reran loadtest. results: p95 -> 188ms, OOMs -> 0. throughput small drop (~3%).

miriam: ```
# reproduce locally
REDWOOD_ALLOC_SOFT_RESERVE=0 ./bin/perf-run --model gpt-large --concurrency 1200 --seq 1024
```

raj: nice. that confirms allocator reservations were the dominant factor. we should still handle kernel fallbacks: if kernel_selector flips to fp32 frequently, we should prefer a slightly slower fp8 kernel that avoids upcast, to reduce memory/latency tail. Add a metric: kernel_fallback_rate per model.

anna: propose combined mitigation:
- default soft_reserve -> dynamic (based on recent max_seq and model quantization type)
- implement per-model kv_cache_dtype hinting (AWQ/GPTQ -> prefer float16 unless kernel requires upcast)
- add kernel_fallback_rate and allocator_fragmentation_ratio to Console dashboards

dave: also add a compacting pass when fragmentation ratio > threshold (threadsafe incremental compaction) — cheap and low-risk. unit test: simulate alternating small/large seq patterns and assert fragmentation stays < 12%.

raj: I'll draft a small change: make soft_reserve opt-in per deployment and add an env var heuristic: REDWOOD_ALLOC_DYNAMIC_RESERVE=1. Will also add the kernel_fallback_rate metric (counter).

deploy-bot: deploy job 6789 started for raj/allocator-heuristic (staging). :rocket:

miriam: after disabling soft_reserve we are back to baseline latencies. please schedule A/B on a dedicated pool before making default change for hosted. We should warn customers using fp8 with big seqs.

anna: noted, I'll write the customer-facing note + internal rollout docs.

raj: action items: (1) PR for dynamic reserve + metric (2) compacting pass spike test (3) KV dtype hinting RFC. I'll assign and link PRs here when ready.

miriam: thanks — saved the cluster from more OOM noise. :thumbsup:
